Ellie — great to connect. Appreciate the procurement template; I attached our latest rate card (redwood_ratecard_v2.xlsx) for your SOW. High-level answers below; Rishi and Marissa are copied for details and commercial options.

High-level:
- Responses vs Chat Completions: Responses is our newer, simpler endpoint family. Pricing is per-generation token for Responses and per-input+output tokens for Chat Completions on the chat-completions endpoint. The unit math is the same (tokens) but the SKU names differ on the invoice.
- Legacy endpoints: We still support legacy completions endpoints; they map 1:1 to a Completions SKU in the rate card.
- Streaming: streaming output is billed by tokens generated; there is no separate streaming surcharge.
- Caching/prefix: automatic prefix cache reduces compute but tokens that are sent to the model for new generation are billed. If you enable prefix caching on shared prompts it can reduce effective billed tokens in steady-state.

Quick ask for accuracy: can you confirm if your 30M/month is counted as total tokens (in+out) or just model-output tokens? That helps Rishi give an apples-to-apples cost estimate.

Attachments: redwood_ratecard_v2.xlsx

Ellie — quick, concrete breakdown (numeric examples to paste into procurement):
1) Billable unit = tokens. We invoice by SKU: responses.unit, chat-completions.unit, completions.legacy. Each SKU has a per-1k-token rate on the attached rate card.

2) Token accounting: input + output tokens are summed for Chat Completions and legacy completions SKUs. Responses SKU bills only on generated tokens (model output) for the primary generation call; if you pass long input contexts they are not double-counted across multiple calls unless re-sent.

3) Conversion examples (approx):
- Single short chat turn (user 25 tokens, model reply 120 tokens):
  - Chat Completions billing = 145 tokens billed (input+output)
  - Responses billing = 120 tokens billed (output only)
  - Legacy completions = billed similar to Chat Completions when used in completion-mode.

4) Streaming: tokens streamed are billed as they are emitted. There is no separate per-stream charge.

5) Caching/prefix: if you enable prefix/KV caching, and the runtime can serve the reply from cache without model compute, you will not be billed for model-generation tokens for that reply. However, cache population calls are billed when they generate tokens. Practically, pilots see ~10-30% token reduction once hot prefixes stabilize.

6) Billing increments: we round billing to the nearest 1 token on the invoice; you will see per-SKU aggregated 1k-token buckets for rate application. No per-request minimums.

Sample cost math (using numbers from redwood_ratecard_v2.xlsx):
- Responses SKU: $0.006 / 1k output tokens -> your 30M output tokens/month = (30,000 * $0.006) = $180/month (note: this is illustrative; actual numbers vary by model tier).
- Chat-completions SKU: $0.008 / 1k tokens (input+output) -> same exchange with higher effective tokens billed.

If you want an exact quote I can run your sample logs through our cost estimator; please send a small sample (one day's logs or 500 representative calls).

Attachment: billing-conversion-guide.pdf

—Rishi
Product Finance — Redwood Inference
